title: How to Actually Start Shopify Dropshipping in 2026
summary: A dropshipping coach walks beginners through an AI store builder, data-driven product picks, supplier sync, AI-generated UGC ads and a Meta campaign, blaming most failures on execution order rather than the model.

assertions.quote: That's why 80 to 90% stores don't make it past their first few months. Not because the model is broken, but because they started wrong.

verdicts.note: Execution matters, but rising ad costs, copycat competition and thin margins are structural features of dropshipping that sink well-executed stores too.

assertions.quote: You're just a middleman with a storefront where the money comes in before money goes out.

verdicts.note: True for inventory, but ad spend, tools and refunds are paid up front, so cash still goes out before most stores see revenue.

assertions.quote: It even shows you which products are taking off before they get saturated.

verdicts.note: Sales-tracking tools do show existing demand, but the same data is visible to every subscriber, so validated products are already contested.

assertions.quote: They make the sale, then they realize that their supplier is slow, unreliable, and shipping takes over a month.

verdicts.note: Long shipping times are the main driver of dropshipping disputes and payment-processor holds, which is well documented by platforms and sellers.

assertions.quote: when a visitor does come to your website, trust gets decided in the first 2 seconds.

verdicts.note: Web credibility research supports fast first impressions, but the effect size on conversion for dropshipping stores is not independently measured.

assertions.quote: You win by testing a bunch at the same time and letting the data tell you which ones are actually working

verdicts.note: Creative testing is standard practice and improves odds, but it multiplies the budget required and most tests still lose money.

assertions.quote: create UGC style video reviews without hiring a single creator.

verdicts.note: The tools produce usable video cheaply, but synthetic testimonials raise platform-policy and consumer-protection problems and there is no independent evidence they convert like real ones.

assertions.quote: you should be leaving detailed targeting completely blank.

verdicts.note: Broad targeting is the platform's own recommendation and works for conversion-optimised campaigns with enough budget, but small accounts often lack the data for it to learn.

assertions.quote: for ROAS, here you want anything above 2.0 because that probably means that you're going to be in a good amount of profit.

verdicts.note: Return on ad spend must exceed the inverse of the margin after goods and fees; this is basic unit economics.

assertions.quote: my students crossing over $50 million combined and counting

verdicts.note: Vendor-reported aggregate revenue with no audit, no count of students who paid, and revenue is not profit.

Empire consistently claimed hundreds of clients generating over $150 million in revenue; the FTC alleges this was false and most clients lost money, so this type of aggregate-sales claim was fabricated in at least this case.
